cells.tense: The pictures being worked from carry weight now, because what has been lived through has been chewed over.
cells.ask: Name one piece of your own experience you're actually finished with, quietly, and let that be the ground you plan from this week.
cells.core:
Holding a large unfinished picture without needing it resolved — that's the shape of this. Enough of the road is lit to take the step in front of you, and you take it. The rest stays dark and that's fine. The pictures you're working from have weight behind them, because what you've lived through has been chewed over and put down rather than carried around whole.

Nothing is being forced. When you finish something off this week, or hand it to someone, notice whether it's coming from a place that has settled or a place that's scrambling. The picture doesn't need more clarity than it has. It needs you standing on what you've already been through, and letting the next bit arrive on its own time.
cells.sheetLine: What you see now is built on what you've already lived through.

cells.tense: The vision is running ahead of any ground it could stand on.
cells.ask: Take one plan you keep rehearsing and do only today's physical step of it — one call, one page, one trip — and stop there.
cells.core:
Standing in the middle of an unfinished thing without forcing it — that's the steady version. You hold the big picture loosely and let the path show itself a step at a time. You don't need to see the whole road; you need the bit under your feet, and it comes.

The bend is that the picture has taken over. You're living in a version of this that hasn't happened — you can feel how the finished thing lands, and details show up in it you haven't earned. Meanwhile what's actually growing goes untended, because tending it is slower than imagining it done. Let one thing be smaller than your picture of it and still worth doing today.

cells.tense: The symbolic door was walked past a while back and is still standing there.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you noticed today with no explanation attached — the image or the hunch, and then stop writing.
cells.core:
Ease with not-knowing is what this looks like when it's working. An impression lands, you act on it, and it turns out accurate without your having argued for it first. You can sit in fog and still pick out what matters, and you don't need to see why before you move.

Right now that channel is pinched. Images, hunches, the sense that something matters — those get filed as not serious, not evidence. So you work with what can be measured and the rest goes unread. This isn't a shortage of imagination. Don't try to dream bigger. Start smaller — one impression a day, written down, unexplained. It doesn't have to prove itself to come back.

cells.tense: The dreaming is running, and it's being filed under something else's name.
cells.ask: Once today, say out loud that a choice in front of you is yours, then make it however you were already going to.
cells.core:
Knowing which pictures are yours is how this looks when you're holding it. What a good life looks like, what you owe people, what would count as having made it — those held on purpose, looked at, redrawn when they've stopped fitting. The pictures shape what gets built and you're the one holding the pen.

The bend is that they're running things from behind the curtain instead. You'd describe them as just how things are. They're yours either way — you drew them somewhere along the line. No announcement needed and nothing to rebuild. Just catch one of them in the act and call it what it is: a picture you're holding, not the shape of the world.
cells.sheetLine: The pictures steering you are yours and can be redrawn.
